stories.headline: Thomson Reuters launches its own LLM, 'Thomson', trained for $40M on an open Chinese base

key_facts.fact: Thomson Reuters announced on August 24, 2026 the launch of Thomson, its first proprietary large language model, developed in-house.
key_facts.excerpt: TORONTO, Aug. 24, 2026 /CNW/ -- Thomson Reuters (Nasdaq: TRI) (TSX: TRI), a global content and technology company, today announced the launch of Thomson, the company's first proprietary large language model, developed in-house.

key_facts.fact: The company says it started from 'a strong open-source foundation' and invested $40 million in talent and compute, versus the billions frontier labs spend.
key_facts.excerpt: Frontier labs have typically spent billions of dollars on compute and years of infrastructure investment to reach the frontier. Thomson Reuters took a different path: starting from a strong open-source foundation and investing $40 million to train Thomson.

key_facts.fact: CTO Joel Hron said Thomson starts from a model called Snowdon, derived from realigning Alibaba's open-weight Qwen; Business Insider identified the base as Qwen3.5.
key_facts.excerpt: Joel Hron, the chief technology officer, told Business Insider that Thomson starts from a model called Snowdon. Snowdon came out of 'realigning' an open-source Qwen model from Alibaba. Business Insider identified the base as Qwen3.5.

key_facts.fact: Thomson's first deployment is inside Tabular Analysis in CoCounsel Legal; a 'small' version ships as open weights on Hugging Face for academic and non-commercial use.
key_facts.excerpt: Thomson's first deployment is inside Tabular Analysis in CoCounsel Legal... Thomson Reuters is also making a 'small' version of Thomson available as an open-weight model on Hugging Face for academic and non-commercial use.

key_facts.fact: CEO Steve Hasker said early internal evaluations put Thomson 'on par with the latest frontier models across a range of tasks', though the release published no figures.
key_facts.excerpt: Steve Hasker, the chief executive, said 'our early evaluations put Thomson on par with the latest frontier models across a range of tasks'. That evaluation is the company's own, and the release publishes no figures alongside it.

key_facts.fact: The launch came a day after legal-AI startup Harvey released Tenet, its first proprietary legal model, post-trained on Moonshot AI's open-weight Kimi K3.
key_facts.excerpt: Harvey launched Tenet on Sunday, its first proprietary model for legal work. Harvey post-trained it on Kimi K3, the open-weight model from the Chinese lab Moonshot AI.

sources.title: Thomson Reuters Leverages its World-Class Data Assets to Launch Its Own Frontier Model
Thomson Reuters Leverages its World-Class Data Assets to Launch Its Own Frontier Model
Thomson Reuters built its own model on a Chinese open base

stories.headline: Perplexity launches Portable Computer, an AI agent that runs fully on-device with zero token cost

key_facts.fact: Perplexity launched Portable Computer on August 25, 2026, a local version of its agentic Computer platform that runs on Nvidia's DGX Spark desktop and Linux machines with RTX GPUs.
key_facts.excerpt: Perplexity is launching Portable Computer today, a version of its agentic 'Computer' platform that runs entirely on hardware users already own — starting with Nvidia's DGX Spark desktop supercomputer and Linux machines equipped with Nvidia RTX GPUs.

key_facts.fact: Work completed locally consumes no billing credits; every task starts on the device by default and the system asks permission before sending a step to a cloud frontier model.
key_facts.excerpt: Work completed locally consumes no billing credits, and the company says every task starts on the device by default — with the system asking permission before sending any individual step to a more powerful frontier model in the cloud.

key_facts.fact: At launch users can run Qwen 3.8 27B or PPLX 27B, a version Perplexity post-trained on its own harness, with Nvidia's Nemotron 3.5 Lightning coming soon.
key_facts.excerpt: At launch, users can set up Qwen 3.8 27B or PPLX 27B, a version Perplexity has post-trained on its own harness, with Nvidia's Nemotron 3.5 Lightning coming soon.

key_facts.fact: On Terminal Bench 2.1 the fully local Qwen model scored 59.6% at near-zero marginal cost; escalating to a Claude Opus 5 cloud 'advisor' raised it to 73.0% at about $0.415 per task, versus 82.4% at $0.65 for the frontier model alone.
key_facts.excerpt: On Terminal Bench 2.1... the fully local Qwen model scored 59.6% at essentially zero marginal cost. Letting it escalate to a Claude Opus 5 'advisor' in the cloud raised the score to 73.0% at an estimated $0.415 per task. Running the frontier model alone scored 82.4% at $0.65 per task.

key_facts.fact: Availability is for Pro, Max, Enterprise Pro and Enterprise Max subscribers on Linux, with Windows in September; any RTX GPU with at least 24GB of VRAM qualifies.
key_facts.excerpt: Portable Computer arrives today for Pro, Max, Enterprise Pro, and Enterprise Max subscribers on Linux, with Windows support following in September. Any RTX GPU with at least 24GB of VRAM — roughly a GeForce RTX 3090 or newer — clears the bar.

key_facts.fact: Before any cloud advisor call, the harness runs a PII classifier over the outgoing context and shows the user exactly what would leave the device; the remote model returns text guidance only.
key_facts.excerpt: Before any advisor call, the harness runs a PII classifier over the outgoing context and shows the user exactly what would leave the device. The remote model returns text guidance only; it never touches local files or tools.

key_facts.fact: The Verge notes Portable Computer runs models fully locally and asks permission before reaching the cloud 'for more advanced research and reasoning'.
key_facts.excerpt: the Portable Computer feature runs AI models fully locally and will ask for permission if it needs to access the cloud 'for more advanced research and reasoning.'

Perplexity's new Portable Computer runs 'entirely on device'

stories.headline: Meta plans to launch 'Hatch' consumer AI agent within weeks and a new model, Watermelon, in October

key_facts.fact: Internal documents reviewed by The Information show Meta plans to launch an AI agent platform codenamed Hatch in late August or early September, and a new model codenamed Watermelon in October.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta Platforms will launch its AI agent Hatch in the coming weeks and release a new AI model called Watermelon in October. That's according to internal documents seen by The Information.

key_facts.fact: Hatch is a consumer version of the OpenClaw agent and part of Zuckerberg's plan to monetize Meta's AI spending beyond advertising, with a tiered pricing model reaching up to $199.99 a month.
key_facts.excerpt: Hatch is set to become a consumer version of the OpenClaw agent and is part of CEO Mark Zuckerberg's plan to make money off the company's heavy AI spending... Meta is weighing a tiered pricing model, including a premium subscription that runs up to $199.99 a month.

key_facts.fact: Hatch is designed to operate on sites including DoorDash, Etsy, Reddit, Yelp and Outlook, with a customizable dashboard offering features like a fitness tracker or trip planner.
key_facts.excerpt: Hatch is designed to tap into sites like DoorDash, Etsy, Reddit, Yelp, and Outlook, and to offer a customizable dashboard with features like a fitness tracker or trip planner.

key_facts.fact: It is not yet clear whether Watermelon will join Meta's Muse model family or ship as a standalone system; Meta declined to comment on the plans.
key_facts.excerpt: It remains unclear whether the model will join Meta's Muse family or be introduced separately... A spokesperson for the company declined to comment on the plans.

key_facts.fact: Meta had banned internal use of OpenClaw, the viral agent tool Hatch is derived from, citing security concerns.
key_facts.excerpt: It is reportedly [inspired] by OpenClaw, a viral agentic tool... The connection is particularly striking given that [Meta] banned internal use [of] OpenClaw... citing security concerns.

stories.headline: AI security company Alice raises $140M as red-teaming for frontier labs nears $100M ARR

key_facts.fact: Alice, an AI trust, safety and security company, announced on August 25, 2026 a $140 million round led by Apax Digital Funds, bringing total funding to $280 million.
key_facts.excerpt: NEW YORK, August 25, 2026 (Newswire.com) - Alice, an AI trust, safety, and security company, today announced a $140 million funding round led by the Apax Digital Funds... The round brings total funding to $280 million. Apax Digital will join the company's board.

key_facts.fact: The company is approaching $100 million in ARR, with its AI business growing more than 500% over the past two years.
key_facts.excerpt: The company is approaching $100 million in ARR, with its AI business growing more than 500% over the past two years.

key_facts.fact: Alice, formerly ActiveFence, runs an AI security lab of more than 150 researchers, works with 8 of the 10 leading AI model labs and protects more than 3 billion people online.
key_facts.excerpt: Alice is home to one of the world's largest AI security research labs, where more than 150 researchers study how AI systems can be manipulated or fail... Alice protects more than 3 billion people online and works with 8 of the 10 leading AI model labs.

key_facts.fact: Before a model ships, Alice's researchers work with frontier labs including Anthropic, Google and Cohere, simulating malicious prompts and agentic tasks to harden models against jailbreaks and prompt injection.
key_facts.excerpt: Before a model is released, Alice's researchers work with frontier labs, including Anthropic, Google, and Cohere, simulating malicious prompts and agentic tasks to surface unpredictable behavior and harden models against jailbreaks and prompt injection.

key_facts.fact: Samsung, SentinelOne, Maj Invest, MoreTech and Phoenix joined the round alongside existing investors including CRV, Norwest, NFX and Highland Europe.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung, SentinelOne, Maj Invest, MoreTech and Phoenix Insurance participated in the round alongside existing investors Resolute Ventures, Grove Ventures, CRV, Highland Europe, Vintage Investments, Norwest, NFX and Claltech.

key_facts.fact: Its platform is built on Rabbit Hole, which the company calls the world's largest dataset of real-world adversarial and harmful content, assembled from a decade tracking fraud, extremism and coordinated manipulation.
key_facts.excerpt: That work produced Rabbit Hole, the world's largest dataset of real-world adversarial and harmful content, which lets Alice recognize attack patterns in AI systems that it has already seen elsewhere.

stories.headline: Anandkumar's Accelerated Understanding unveils a physics AI that ate 5 trillion data points in one prompt

key_facts.fact: Accelerated Understanding Inc launched publicly on Tuesday, August 25, 2026, unveiling an AI model built for physics rather than language.
key_facts.excerpt: A research duo, once pitched to lead the Jeff Bezos-backed Project Prometheus, on Tuesday unveiled what they've built on their own: an AI model that can take in and produce information so vast that a lone computer might not handle it.

key_facts.fact: The company says its model handled 5 trillion pieces of data in a single prompt in tests, roughly 5 million times what flagship Anthropic and Google models typically consume.
key_facts.excerpt: Their company, Accelerated Understanding Inc, says it has developed a different type of AI model that in tests handled 5 trillion pieces of data in a single prompt. That is some 5 million times the size of what Anthropic and Google's flagship models can typically consume.

key_facts.fact: The system drops the Transformer architecture entirely and instead uses neural operators, a technique co-founder Anima Anandkumar helped pioneer, to predict physical phenomena in space and time.
key_facts.excerpt: It dispensed with the Google-invented Transformer architecture — the 'T' in ChatGPT — and instead processes physics data based on technology that Anandkumar helped pioneer years ago, called neural operators.

key_facts.fact: Co-founders Anima Anandkumar, a Caltech professor and former Nvidia director, and Benedikt Jenik turned down a Project Prometheus offer that included a 35% stake, up to $2M combined salary and more than $2 billion in committed capital.
key_facts.excerpt: the proposal said Anandkumar could be the public face of the company, a board member, and owner of its scientific vision... The offer letter outlined more than $2 billion in capital for what the letter called 'committed rounds' of financing through Series B, from investors including Bezos.

key_facts.fact: Bezos and Vik Bajaj went on to raise a $12 billion Series B for Prometheus in June 2026, targeting AI that automates manufacturing of complex physical systems.
key_facts.excerpt: Anandkumar and Jenik ultimately kept building solo, while Bezos and Bajaj went on to raise a $12 billion Series B for Prometheus in June 2026. Prometheus is targeting AI that can automate the manufacturing of complex physical systems.

key_facts.fact: Target applications include chip design, robotics, extreme weather prediction and geological data for energy companies, replacing bespoke math models with one physics AI.
key_facts.excerpt: The company also thinks the same AI can power robotics, predict extreme weather, or sift through geological data for energy companies. Instead of brittle and bespoke math models for each, one AI can handle any physics query for the business world.

sources.title: Exclusive: The AI founders who walked away from Bezos-backed Prometheus to model the universe
AI experts that were going to build 'Prometheus' for Jeff Bezos build new machine to understand the universe instead

stories.headline: OpenAI bans Russian ChatGPT accounts running a fake institute and a pro-Moscow 'sovereignty index'

key_facts.fact: OpenAI said on Tuesday, August 25, 2026 that it had banned a cluster of ChatGPT accounts originating in Russia used to support a covert online influence campaign.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI said on Tuesday it had banned pro-Russia ChatGPT accounts that were being used in an online 'influence campaign.'

key_facts.fact: The company found the operation after investigating AI-generated social media posts, which led it to a 'much broader influence operation', disclosed in a blog post.
key_facts.excerpt: The company discovered the issue after investigating AI-generated social media posts, which led it to a 'much broader influence operation,' OpenAI said in a blog post on Tuesday.

key_facts.fact: The campaign was built around a website with copied and misattributed academic work, a 'sovereignty' index favorable to Russia, and efforts to disguise the operators' Russian origins.
key_facts.excerpt: The campaign was 'built around a website containing copied and misattributed academic work, a 'sovereignty' index that cast Russia in a favourable light, and efforts to disguise the operators' Russian origins.'

key_facts.fact: Operators prompted in Russian to generate comments posted on Substack, Telegram, X, Facebook and LinkedIn, instructing ChatGPT to hide linguistic clues that they were Russian; much of the content promoted a body called the International Burke Institute.
key_facts.excerpt: The operators prompted in Russian to generate social media comments that were posted on Substack, Telegram, X, Facebook and LinkedIn, and instructed ChatGPT to hide any linguistic clues that they were Russian... Much of the content generated promoted an organization called the International Burke Institute (IBI).

key_facts.fact: OpenAI does not offer access to its models in Russia; the operators used VPNs to disguise their location, and the campaign's immediate reach was limited.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI does not allow access to its models in Russia, but the company said VPNs were used to disguise location... While the immediate impact of the operation [was] limited, the company added, the 'significance of the operation lies less in the audience it reached, however, than in the infrastructure it had built.'

key_facts.fact: OpenAI also banned a group linked to a Chinese technology company with government ties that sought to shape U.S. policy discussions, and Chinese-speaking users generating anti-Trump slogans, cartoons and multilingual comments.
key_facts.excerpt: Another group linked to a Chinese technology company with government ties allegedly sought to shape U.S. policy discussions. OpenAI also banned Chinese-speaking users who used ChatGPT to create anti-Trump slogans, cartoons and multilingual comments for social media and news platforms.

stories.headline: Musk tells Cursor staff Grok has fallen behind and calls Anthropic the leader of the AI race

key_facts.fact: The Information reported on August 24, 2026, citing five people familiar with the meeting, that Musk used his first all-hands with Cursor employees to say SpaceX's AI division had fallen behind rivals.
key_facts.excerpt: On the day SpaceX confirmed it had completed its $60 billion acquisition of the AI coding startup, Musk dialled into an all-hands video call and told more than 1,000 Cursor employees that SpaceX's AI division had slipped behind its rivals, according to a report in The Information citing five people with knowledge of the meeting.

key_facts.fact: Musk said Tesla and SpaceX lead their markets but Grok does not, that it 'desperately needs to catch up', and that he was 'not used to losing'.
key_facts.excerpt: The premise of what he was trying to communicate was that Tesla and SpaceX are 'dominant' players where they do business, while his AI company, xAI, had 'fallen behind'... 'Grok isn't the leader in its market, and it desperately needs to catch up, he said'.

key_facts.fact: He singled out Anthropic as the current leader in the AI race and a formidable competitor — an awkward concession given reports that xAI engineers reached for Claude to code.
key_facts.excerpt: Musk said Anthropic was leading the AI race and was a strong rival, one person told The Information. That is an awkward thing to concede when earlier reporting suggested xAI's own engineers reached for Claude when they wanted to code.

key_facts.fact: Musk told the room AI models will eventually become too advanced for humans to control, which is why he wants his side to build them first, and pledged SpaceX would keep stockpiling more compute than any rival.
key_facts.excerpt: Musk also supposedly said AI models are sure to become too advanced for humanity to control, so he considers it necessary that SpaceX 'build the technology before other companies did'.

key_facts.fact: Cursor reportedly crossed $2 billion in annualized revenue in June, but 45 people, mostly from product and engineering, have left since April, including about 20 who arrived via the Graphite acquisition.
key_facts.excerpt: It reportedly crossed $[2] billion in annualised revenue in June, and headcount has more [than] quadrupled over the past year... But 45 people, mostly from product and engineering, have left since April, The Information reports, including roughly 20 who arrived through the Graphite acquisition.

key_facts.fact: The meeting took place on or around August 15, when SpaceX closed the $60 billion Cursor purchase.
key_facts.excerpt: This meeting was apparently on or around August 15, when SpaceX closed the deal to buy Cursor for $60 billion. Apparently this was Musk's very first time addressing the staff of Cursor in an all-hands.

stories.headline: Apple debuts M6, its first 2nm chip, and the quad-die M5 Ultra, with price hikes on Mac mini and Studio

key_facts.fact: Apple on Aug 25 debuted M6 in a new Mac mini and M5 Ultra in a new Mac Studio; M6 is Apple's first 2-nanometer chip, with a 12-core CPU, 12-core GPU, a Dual 16-core Neural Engine and up to 170GB/s of unified memory bandwidth.
key_facts.excerpt: M6, Apple's first state-of-the-art 2-nanometer chip, advances every compute block... a larger 12-core CPU complex with the world's fastest CPU core, a larger 12-core GPU with Neural Accelerators, a Dual 16-core Neural Engine, and up to 170GB/s of unified memory bandwidth.

key_facts.fact: M5 Ultra uses UltraFusion to connect two dual-die M5 Max chips into Apple's first quad-die SoC, with over 4.4TB/s of inter-die bandwidth, up to a 36-core CPU and an 80-core GPU.
key_facts.excerpt: M5 Ultra uses UltraFusion to connect two dual-die M5 Max chips to form the quad-die architecture — a first for Apple silicon. UltraFusion increases the inter-die bandwidth to over 4.4TB/s and the connection density by over 6x.

key_facts.fact: Mac Studio with M5 Ultra supports up to 512GB of unified memory and 1.2TB/s of memory bandwidth, 50% more than M3 Ultra, letting users run LLMs with hundreds of billions of parameters entirely on device.
key_facts.excerpt: M5 Ultra features a massive amount of high-bandwidth unified memory, up to 512GB, and delivers a staggering 1.2TB/s of unified memory bandwidth that is 50 percent higher than M3 Ultra... run huge LLMs with hundreds of billions of parameters entirely on device.

key_facts.fact: M5 Ultra's 80-core GPU includes a Neural Accelerator in each core, giving up to 4.5x the peak GPU compute for AI compared with M3 Ultra.
key_facts.excerpt: M5 Ultra features a next-generation GPU with up to 80 cores, incorporating a Neural Accelerator in each core to offer up to 4.5x the peak GPU compute for AI compared to M3 Ultra.

key_facts.fact: Prices rose: the M6 Mac mini starts at $899 and the M5 Pro Mac mini at $1,699, each $100 above the M4 models, while the M5 Ultra Mac Studio starts at $5,499, up $200.
key_facts.excerpt: Apple raises Mac mini and Studio prices: the M6 and M5 Pro Mac mini are $899+ and $1,699+, $100 above M4 models, and the M5 Ultra Mac Studio is $5,499+, up $200 (Nicole Nguyen/Wall Street Journal)

key_facts.fact: The new Mac mini models are available for preorder now and ship after September 22.
key_facts.excerpt: Apple's newest Mac Mini devices are available for preorder now, starting at $899. They will ship after September 22.

stories.headline: OpenAI's Jalapeño chip beats Nvidia Blackwell on performance per watt in first public benchmarks

key_facts.fact: OpenAI presented its custom inference chip Jalapeño at Hot Chips and let SemiAnalysis benchmark it; the chip, built with Broadcom, went from team hiring to tape-out in about 16 months.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI has spent the past couple years quietly building 'Jalapeño,' an inference chip just announced at Hot Chips... Design work began in the middle of 2024, going from initial team hiring to manufacturing tape-out in ~16 months, an extremely fast ASIC development cycle.

key_facts.fact: Jalapeño delivered 1.5x to 1.9x more AI work per watt and 1.7x to 3.6x lower latency than Nvidia's Blackwell chips across tests on GPT-OSS, DeepSeek R1 and Kimi K2.5.
key_facts.excerpt: Jalapeño outperformed Blackwell in many scenarios, delivering 1.5 to 1.9 times more AI work per watt and 1.7 to 3.6 times lower latency, especially excelling in both low-latency and high-throughput scenarios.

key_facts.fact: In testing, Jalapeño hit over 700 tokens per second per user at concurrency 1 on DeepSeek R1 and roughly 1,400 tokens/sec/user on GPT-OSS, without speculative decoding or prefill-decode disaggregation.
key_facts.excerpt: At low concurrency scenarios, Jalapeño demonstrates remarkable interactivity, hitting over 700 tokens per sec per user at concurrency 1 on the DeepSeek R1 model... GPT-OSS which ran at approximately 1,400 tok/sec/user... all achieved with single-token prediction (STP), no speculative decoding and no prefill-decode disaggregation.

key_facts.fact: The tested A0 silicon is already succeeded by a B0 stepping in the fab that delivers roughly 25% better performance per watt and 13.4 PFLOPs of MXFP4 on a reticle-sized TSMC N3P compute die, versus 17.5 PFLOPs for a comparable Nvidia Rubin die.
key_facts.excerpt: B0 has optimizations that deliver roughly a 25% perf-per-watt improvement over the earlier A0 silicon. Specifically, the B0 stepping delivers 13.4 PFLOPs of MXFP4 on a single reticle-sized compute die that is manufactured on TSMC's N3P. This compares to 17.5 PFLOPs of dense Rubin NVFP4 for a single Rubin compute die.

key_facts.fact: Jalapeño ships with HBM4, giving 15.4TB/s of memory bandwidth per package, and runs at a 700W TDP versus 900-1,150W for a Rubin compute die.
key_facts.excerpt: Jalapeño will ship with HBM4... This results in 15.4TB/s of memory bandwidth per package which bests all the other accelerators shipping that are using HBM3E... Jalapeño's TDP is only 700W compared to Rubin's at 900-1,150W per compute die.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI and Broadcom first unveiled Jalapeño in June 2026 as an accelerator built from scratch for LLM inference, to be deployed at gigawatt scale with data center partners.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI on Wednesday announced its first custom chip developed with Broadcom. Called Jalapeño and designed by OpenAI, the chip, the companies said, provides better performance per watt than current state-of-the-art chips in early testing.

sources.title: OpenAI' Jalapeño: Better Than Nvidia Blackwell
OpenAI's Jalapeño spices up chip market as it outperforms Nvidia's Blackwell

stories.headline: Nvidia puts Groq 3 LPX inference accelerator into full production, with Nebius as first cloud customer

key_facts.fact: Nvidia announced at Hot Chips on Aug 24 that Groq 3 LPX, an interactive AI inference accelerator extending the Vera Rubin platform, is now in full production.
key_facts.excerpt: Hot Chips—NVIDIA today announced that NVIDIA Groq 3 LPX, the interactive AI inference accelerator, is now in full production. An extension of the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform, Groq 3 LPX delivers a major boost in AI inference by enabling ultrafast token generation for highly responsive agentic systems.

key_facts.fact: In Artificial Analysis benchmarking, Groq 3 LPX ran Gemma 4 31B at a record 3,400 output tokens per second with a 100,000-token context — the fastest ever recorded for that model.
key_facts.excerpt: It delivered a record 3,400 output tokens per second in Artificial Analysis benchmarking running Gemma 4 31B, an open source agentic model, with a 100,000-token context critical for agentic systems — the fastest performance ever recorded for the model.

key_facts.fact: Each LPX rack couples 256 LPU accelerators with 128GB of on-chip SRAM and 640TB/s of scale-up bandwidth, fully liquid-cooled on the Nvidia MGX rack architecture; each LPU has 500MB of SRAM and 150TB/s of SRAM bandwidth.
key_facts.excerpt: Each NVIDIA LPX rack couples 256 LPU accelerators with 128 GB of on-chip SRAM and 640 TB/s of scale-up bandwidth, fully liquid-cooled using the NVIDIA MGX rack architecture.

key_facts.fact: Nebius is the first AI cloud to adopt Groq 3 LPX, bringing it to its Nebius Token Factory inference platform.
key_facts.excerpt: Nebius, a leading AI cloud, plans to bring NVIDIA Groq 3 LPX to Nebius Token Factory, its production inference platform, giving developers access to extreme token generation speed for highly responsive agentic AI applications.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia projects that Vera Rubin NVL72 with LPX delivers up to 35x higher inference throughput per megawatt for 2-trillion-parameter models at long context and low latency than GB200 NVL72.
key_facts.excerpt: With NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72, NVIDIA projects up to 35x higher inference throughput per megawatt for 2T-parameter models at long-context and low-latency than GB200 NVL72.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia also said SpaceXAI is deploying its Vera CPU for agentic AI at massive scale, and Elon Musk said SpaceX and Nvidia designed a space-optimized Vera Rubin NVL72 system for launch to orbit in Q4 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: Elon Musk /@elonmusk: SpaceX, in partnership with Nvidia, has designed a space-optimized Vera Rubin NVL72 system for launch to orbit in Q4 next year, with significant scale in 2028... @nvidianewsroom: The first CPU built for agents is now at work at massive scale. @SpaceXAI is deploying NVIDIA Vera to power agentic AI.

stories.headline: Unitree shares slump 45% after fivefold IPO pop, wiping $30B off the robot maker's value

key_facts.fact: Unitree shares have fallen roughly 45% since their Shanghai debut, steadying on Tuesday Aug 25 after three straight days of decline.
key_facts.excerpt: Unitree shares steadied today after three consecutive days of decline that took their losses to 45% since their debut last Wednesday.

key_facts.fact: The company's valuation soared to $66 billion at one point and later plunged by $30 billion, raising questions about whether AI and robotics enthusiasm has outpaced fundamentals.
key_facts.excerpt: The wild swings in Unitree's valuation - soaring to $66 billion at one point and later plunging by $30 billion - have led to questions about whether enthusiasm for AI and robotics has outpaced fundamentals.

key_facts.fact: Unitree closed up 460% on its Aug 19 debut, against an average first-day gain of 226% for new Chinese listings over the past three years.
key_facts.excerpt: Shares of Unitree, which competes with Tesla and Hyundai Motor Group-owned Boston Dynamics, finished up 460 per cent on its debut. That compares with an average first-day gain of 226 per cent for newly listed stocks in China over the past three years.

key_facts.fact: Analysts blamed China's listing mechanism and the absence of short-sellers; asset manager Dong Baozhen said investors 'were carried away by the technology revolution narrative' and that 'all bubbles are doomed to burst.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'Investors were carried away by the technology revolution narrative,' said Dong Baozhen, chairman of Beijing-based asset manager Lingtong Shengtai, cautioning that 'all bubbles are doomed to burst.'

key_facts.fact: Unitree's first-half 2026 profit showed signs of a downshift and the company has had little success in broader commercial applications despite viral running, dancing and martial-arts robot demos.
key_facts.excerpt: The blockbuster debut came even as Unitree's first-half profit showed signs of a downshift. The company's robots have drawn attention for running, dancing and performing martial arts, but Unitree has had little success in broader commercial applications.

key_facts.fact: Unitree priced its IPO at 150.80 yuan a share and raised about 6.1 billion yuan ($905 million); DeepSeek invested about 140.8 million yuan and Tencent is an existing shareholder.

stories.headline: US launches 'Operation Economic Outcast' against Iran as Trump threatens mine-laying ships

key_facts.fact: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced 'Operation Economic Outcast' on Monday, Aug. 24, sanctioning nearly 60 individuals, entities and vessels and issuing sectoral determinations covering digital assets, technology, gold, aviation and shipping.
key_facts.excerpt: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has unveiled crushing sanctions against almost 60 Iranian entities, individuals and vessels. During the news conference, he also issued determinations against five key sectors: digital assets, technology, gold, aviation and shipping.

key_facts.fact: Bessent said countries that keep trading with Iran risk being forced out of the dollar-based financial system, but he gave no timeline and the list did not include the Chinese financial institutions suspected of facilitating Iran's oil sales.
key_facts.excerpt: While he said countries that continued trading with Iran risked being forced out of the dollar-based financial system, he declined to give a timeline or identify which may be targeted... the list did not feature any of the Chinese financial institutions suspected of facilitating Iran's oil

key_facts.fact: Iran's Economy Minister Ali Madanizadeh said Tehran is 'fully prepared' and has a two-year plan to manage the sanctions, predicting 'another defeat' for Washington.
key_facts.excerpt: "We've been waiting for these plans for a long time, and the government is and was ready and has a two-year plan to manage these events"

key_facts.fact: Trump said on Aug. 25 that the US Navy had removed or detonated all mines from international waters in the Strait of Hormuz and warned that any vessel laying new mines would be 'immediately and systematically destroyed'.
key_facts.excerpt: "I have just been informed by the United States Navy that all mines have been removed and/or detonated from within the International Waters of the Strait of Hormuz," Trump wrote.

key_facts.fact: Iran and Oman issued a joint statement on Tuesday proposing a temporary joint navigational corridor through the Strait of Hormuz and a joint mine-clearing project, with technical talks to continue.
key_facts.excerpt: "The proposed framework includes the establishment of a joint temporary navigational corridor through the Strait of Hormuz and an agreement to implement a joint project to clear the Strait of mines."

key_facts.fact: Iranian oil exports through the strait have fallen from about 2 million barrels per day before the war to roughly 0.4 million bpd by mid-August, according to tracker Kpler, and Treasury sanctioned networks spanning the UAE, Hong Kong, China, Singapore and Europe.
key_facts.excerpt: According to maritime tracker Kpler, Iranian oil exports through the strait have fallen from about two million barrels per day before the war to around 0.4 million barrels per day by mid-August following the US naval blockade.

key_facts.fact: An oil tanker was struck and disabled by an unidentified projectile in the Strait of Hormuz near Oman, according to UK Maritime Trade Operations, while Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth said kinetic strikes remain an option.

stories.headline: FDA approves J&J's Imaavy as the first treatment ever cleared for warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia

key_facts.fact: Johnson & Johnson said on Aug. 24 that the FDA approved Imaavy (nipocalimab-aahu) for warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia in adults and patients 12 and older who are currently or previously treated with corticosteroids — the first therapy proven safe and effective specifically for the disease.
key_facts.excerpt: Johnson & Johnson (NYSE: JNJ) today announced the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval of IMAAVY (nipocalimab-aahu) for the treatment of warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia (wAIHA)... marks the first time a therapy was proven safe and effective specifically for the treatment of wAIHA.

key_facts.fact: wAIHA is a rare, life-threatening disease in which autoantibodies destroy red blood cells, causing severe anemia and debilitating fatigue; Imaavy is an FcRn blocker that reduces pathogenic IgG autoantibodies while preserving B-cell function.
key_facts.excerpt: IMAAVY is an immunoselective FcRn blocker designed to target and reduce pathogenic immunoglobulin G (IgG) autoantibodies while also preserving B-cell function

key_facts.fact: In the placebo-controlled Phase 2/3 ENERGY trial, roughly three times as many patients on the approved dose achieved a durable hemoglobin response by week 24, with a mean hemoglobin increase of 1 g/dL as early as week 1.
key_facts.excerpt: The randomized, placebo-controlled trial demonstrated approximately three times as many patients receiving the approved dose of IMAAVY achieved durable Hgb levels versus placebo by 24 weeks.

key_facts.fact: ENERGY randomized 115 adults roughly 1:1:1 to two nipocalimab dosing schedules or placebo, and patients on the drug scored 3.5 points better on the FACIT-Fatigue scale than placebo at week 24.
key_facts.excerpt: 115 adults were randomized approximately 1:1:1 to receive nipocalimab at two different dose schedules or placebo... IMAAVY was associated with a 3.5-point higher mean FACIT-Fatigue score versus placebo at Week 24

key_facts.fact: The approval followed FDA Priority Review; Imaavy was already approved in the US in April 2025 for generalized myasthenia gravis.
key_facts.excerpt: The approval, which follows FDA Priority Review, marks the first time a therapy was proven safe and effective specifically for the treatment of wAIHA... Imaavy was approved in the United States in April 2025 for the treatment of gMG

key_facts.fact: The most common adverse reactions in wAIHA patients treated with Imaavy were peripheral edema, diarrhea and fever.
key_facts.excerpt: The most common adverse reactions (≥10%) in patients with wAIHA treated with IMAAVY were peripheral edema, diarrhea, and fever.

stories.headline: FDA clears Roche's Alzheimer's blood test for primary care as Leqembi's home autoinjector reaches patients

key_facts.fact: Roche said on Aug. 24 that the FDA cleared its Elecsys Phospho-Tau (217P) Plasma blood test to help identify amyloid pathology associated with Alzheimer's in people 55 and older who show signs of cognitive decline.
key_facts.excerpt: Roche announced today that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has cleared the Elecsys Phospho-Tau (217P) Plasma (pTau217) blood test, providing clinicians across primary and specialty care with a single blood-based option to aid in identifying amyloid pathology

key_facts.fact: Developed with Eli Lilly, it is the first and only FDA-cleared single-biomarker blood test that supports both rule-in and rule-out assessment of amyloid pathology using the same validated cutoffs in primary and specialty care.
key_facts.excerpt: Developed in collaboration with Eli Lilly and Company, Elecsys pTau217 is the first and only FDA-cleared, single-biomarker blood test that supports both rule-in and rule-out assessment of amyloid pathology using the same validated clinical cutoffs across primary and specialty care settings.

key_facts.fact: The same day, Eisai and Biogen announced that the once-weekly Leqembi Iqlik (lecanemab-irmb) subcutaneous autoinjector is now available in the US to start therapy in early Alzheimer's, for adults with mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia.
key_facts.excerpt: Eisai Co., Ltd. and Biogen Inc. (Nasdaq: BIIB), announced today that once weekly lecanemab-irmb subcutaneous injection (brand name: LEQEMBI IQLIK) is now available in the U.S. for initiation therapy for early Alzheimer's disease (AD) in adults

key_facts.fact: The FDA approved the subcutaneous initiation dose on July 13, making Leqembi Iqlik the first anti-amyloid treatment offering at-home dosing for both initiation and maintenance in the US.
key_facts.excerpt: lecanemab-irmb subcutaneous injection (US brand name: Leqembi Iqlik), which was approved by the FDA on July 13, now is available in the US for initiation therapy for early Alzheimer's disease. Leqembi Iqlik is the first-of-its-kind anti-amyloid treatment that offers at-home dosing

key_facts.fact: In the 1,795-patient Clarity AD trial, lecanemab slowed disease progression by 27% versus placebo at 18 months on the CDR-SB scale; the drug is now approved in 53 countries.
key_facts.excerpt: data showed LEQEMBI IV significantly slowed disease progression at 18 months (27% vs placebo)... Lecanemab has been approved in 53 countries and regions

stories.headline: FDA halts Regenxbio's Hunter syndrome gene therapy after spinal MRI findings in five patients

key_facts.fact: Regenxbio announced on Aug. 24 that the FDA placed a clinical hold on the investigational new drug application for its Phase I/II/III trial of RGX-121 for Mucopolysaccharidosis type II (Hunter syndrome).
key_facts.excerpt: On August 24, 2026, REGENXBIO Inc. announced that it received communication from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration that the Company's Investigational New Drug application for its Phase I/II/III trial of RGX-121 for Mucopolysaccharidosis type II ('MPS II'), also known as Hunter Syndrome, was placed on clinical hold

key_facts.fact: The company said it does not expect to resubmit the RGX-121 Biologics License Application in the near term.
key_facts.excerpt: the company does not expect to resubmit the RGX-121 Biologics License Application in the near term

key_facts.fact: The hold followed the discovery of asymptomatic spine MRI findings — a small nodule or small cystic mass — in five participants of the CAMPSIITE study who were dosed roughly three to six years ago; no brain nodules or masses were found.
key_facts.excerpt: identified asymptomatic findings of either a small nodule or a small cystic mass in spine MRIs of five participants who received intracisternal or intraventricular RGX-121 approximately three to six years ago... No brain nodules or masses were identified on any brain MRIs.

key_facts.fact: Investigators deemed the findings nonserious and radiologists believe they are likely benign, with all five patients showing stability to improvement on neurocognitive and neurobehavioral assessments.
key_facts.excerpt: All five participants continue to do well clinically and have demonstrated overall stability to improvement on neurocognitive and neurobehavioral assessments... Investigators deemed these findings to be nonserious and radiologists believe they are likely benign

key_facts.fact: The findings surfaced through an expanded brain-and-spine MRI monitoring plan the company put in place a few months ago following an earlier clinical hold on its RGX-111 program.
key_facts.excerpt: The findings were identified through an expanded MRI monitoring plan, implemented by REGENXBIO a few months ago, following the clinical hold related to RGX-111.

key_facts.fact: CEO Curran Simpson said the company believes the findings are unique to the Hunter syndrome program and remains on track to submit its Duchenne muscular dystrophy BLA this quarter, with wet AMD pivotal data due in Q4.
key_facts.excerpt: "We believe these findings are unique and limited to our Hunter Syndrome program... We remain focused on our Duchenne and retinal disease candidates... including the planned submission of the Duchenne BLA this quarter and the wet AMD topline pivotal data announcement in the fourth quarter."

key_facts.excerpt: Liftoff from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station happened at 5:33 a.m. EDT (0933 UTC).

key_facts.fact: The first stage, tail number B1067, made its 37th flight — a reuse record — after entering service in June 2021, and landed on the droneship A Shortfall of Gravitas about 8.5 minutes after liftoff.

key_facts.fact: It could be the last Starlink flight from Cape Canaveral for a while, with the Florida workforce refocused on Starship preparations; 44 of SpaceX's 76 Starlink missions this year have flown from Vandenberg.

The company's Cape Canaveral workforce has been refocused on Starship preparations.
